summary: auth-service began failing ~1/3 of token validations with 401 invalid_token at ~14:01, immediately after two co-timed changes: deploy dep-5710 (JWT library upgrade jjwt 0.11→0.12, TokenValidator rewritten, 14:00) and config change cfg-2705 (JWT signing-key rotation k-2025-10→k-2026-04, 14:01). Resources (CPU ~38%, memory ~52%, no restarts), request rate (~400 rps) and latency (~90ms p99) are all flat, ruling out resource/capacity/infra causes; user-db and redis-cache are quiet. The fault originates in auth-service. A bad_deployment (faulty new TokenValidator / library upgrade) is best supported, closely followed by a config_change (key rotation / JWKS propagation). Because the two changes are 60s apart and auth-service's own logs are unavailable (identity-namespace pipeline down), I cannot fully separate them; timing alone is ambiguous, so I rank the deploy first on shape and historical symptom match but flag the rotation as a live alternative.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bad deploy: auth-service v7.3.0 JWT library/TokenValidator regression rejects valid tokens
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 14:00 deployment dep-5710 upgraded jjwt 0.11->0.12 (breaking parser API) and rewrote TokenValidator. The new validation path rejects a stable ~1/3 of otherwise-valid tokens with 401 invalid_token, producing persistent errors from ~14:01 until the current time.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5710 deployed auth-service v7.3.0 at 14:00 with jjwt 0.11->0.12 and a rewritten TokenValidator
New validation logic rejects tokens -> 401 invalid_token at api-gateway

assumptions: The new TokenValidator has a bug (e.g., algorithm/claim/clock-skew handling) that rejects a token class
cfg-2705 at 14:01 is not the actual trigger
~36% corresponds to the fraction of pods/requests hitting the new code path

ranked_hypotheses.title: Config change: JWT signing-key rotation cfg-2705 broke token validation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: At 14:01 cfg-2705 rotated jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04. If the new key id was published before all pods loaded the JWKS (per HIST-108), tokens signed/verified against the wrong key fail, yielding 401 invalid_token.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2705 rotated the signing key id at 14:01
Pods/consumers with stale or missing key verify against wrong key -> 401 invalid_token

assumptions: JWKS propagation lag or a wrong key causes mismatches
The rotation, not the deploy, is causal

ranked_hypotheses.title: Resource/capacity or infrastructure failure in auth path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: auth-service or its datastores ran out of CPU/memory/connections, or redis/user-db failed, causing validation failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU ~38%, memory ~52%, latency ~90ms, request rate ~400rps and restarts=0 are all flat with no step change at onset; user-db 0 errors; redis only 3 unrelated WARNs. No resource or infra degradation correlates with onset.

facts.statement: auth-service error rate was ~0.2% until 13:58, jumped to 24.86% in the 14:01 bucket and stabilized at ~36% from 14:04 onward.
api-gateway first logged 'auth-service POST /v1/token/validate -> 401 invalid_token' at 14:02:22Z, with 466 such events through 15:58:51Z.

The only relevant changes are deploy dep-5710 (auth-service v7.3.0, 14:00Z, 'jjwt 0.11 -> 0.12 (breaking parser API)', 'TokenValidator rewritten', status live, not rolled back) and config change cfg-2705 (jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04, 14:01Z).
auth-service CPU (~38%), memory (~52%), latency p99 (~90ms) and request_rate (~400 req/s) are flat across the incident; restarts are 0.
user-db logged 0 ERROR entries and redis-cache logged only 3 unrelated WARNs (clock drift, slow /internal/metrics, GC pause) in the window.

Historical incident HIST-109 matches symptoms exactly (401 invalid_token after JWT library upgrade, category bad_deployment) and HIST-108 matches a key-rotation cause (401s after signing key rotation, category config_change).
auth-service logs became fully unavailable (query_logs returned 503 then circuit_open) and api-gateway logs contain no 'signature', 'key', or 'expired' strings.

assumptions: Onset is ~14:00-14:02 (error_rate bucket boundary at 14:01 plus first gateway 401 at 14:02:22).
The generic 'invalid_token' gateway message hides the auth-service-side failure reason (signature vs parse vs key-not-found).
No other change (market-data-service dep-5699 at 11:35) is relevant to token validation.
Historical incidents are analogous patterns, not proof of the current cause.

timeline.event: market-data-service dep-5699 v5.0.3 deployed (Fix symbol mapping) - unrelated, pre-onset.
auth-service dep-5710 v7.3.0 deployed: jjwt 0.11->0.12 (breaking parser API), TokenValidator rewritten.
Config change cfg-2705: jwt.signing.key_id k-2025-10 -> k-2026-04 (scheduled key rotation). error_rate bucket 14:01 rises to avg 24.86%.
First 401 invalid_token on auth-service /v1/token/validate logged at api-gateway.
auth-service error_rate stabilizes ~36% and remains flat through 15:59.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back auth-service to the pre-dep-5710 version (or pin jjwt to 0.11) and observe whether 401 invalid_token rate returns to baseline.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deploy precedes onset by ~1-2 minutes and is the best-supported trigger; rollback both tests the bad-deployment hypothesis and (if it clears the errors) restores service.

recommended_actions.action: If rollback does not clear the 401s, re-publish the previous signing key id (k-2025-10) / fix JWKS propagation for cfg-2705.
recommended_actions.rationale: Tests the alternative config_change hypothesis (HIST-108 pattern: key rotated before all pods loaded JWKS).

recommended_actions.action: Capture/auth-service-side error detail (signature mismatch vs parse/claim error) by restoring the identity-namespace log pipeline or adding a distinct error code at the gateway.
recommended_actions.rationale: The generic 'invalid_token' message is insufficient to separate a key mismatch from a library regression; this is the key discriminator.

recommended_actions.action: Stage key rotations and gate JWT-library upgrades so only one change lands at a time; add JWKS-load confirmation before publishing a new key id.
recommended_actions.rationale: Both prior incidents (HIST-108/HIST-109) stem from these change classes; co-timed changes made diagnosis ambiguous.

data_gaps: auth-service logs are unavailable (identity-namespace pipeline down; query_logs returned 503 then circuit_open) so the auth-side failure reason for invalid_token cannot be read.
api-gateway logs expose only the generic 'invalid_token' text; no 'signature'/'key'/'expired' detail to distinguish key mismatch from a parser/library bug.
Deploy dep-5710 rollout state (how many replicas run the new version) is unknown, so the '~1/3 of pods' mechanism for the 36% rate is unverified.
No rollback has been attempted, so causal confirmation (error rate normalizing on rollback) is not yet available.
kyc-provider (external dependency) has no telemetry, so it cannot be fully excluded as a contributor, though the failure is in token validation which does not involve it.
